module: D09-13 Industry Structure／Porter Five Forces產業結構與波特五力

theorySources.use: Concentration is an imperfect indicator; combine with prices, markups, profits, entry and other competitive-intensity evidence.
Firm resources/capabilities are a competing/complementary explanation to industry structure.

mechanisms: A structurally attractive industry may sustain pricing or returns on invested capital when rivalry, entry, substitute and bargaining pressures are persistently weak.
Industry structure can shape how value is divided between producers, suppliers and customers rather than simply determining revenue growth.
Capacity additions, qualification cycles and switching costs can change force strength over time; the framework must be time-varying rather than static.
falsification: High concentration alone does not prove weak competition or superior profitability; market definition may be wrong and efficient/intangible-intensive leaders can create concentration while prices still fall.
Attractive industry structure does not guarantee a specific issuer wins; firm resources, execution, customer mix and capital allocation can dominate cross-sectional outcomes.
Fast technology substitution can destroy apparent barriers before accounting data reveals it.
Cyclical scarcity can temporarily mimic structural pricing power; a boom-period margin spike is not durable evidence of entry barriers.
Regulation can both raise entry barriers and cap profitability; barrier direction and shareholder-value direction are not identical.

redundancyControls: Do not double-count Pricing Power from D10-06 as an independent D09-13 vote; treat it as one observable consequence.
Do not duplicate D09-10 concentration metrics without new structural interpretation.
Separate company moat/resource evidence from industry-structure evidence.

systemUse.System1: Context/reject-confounding research only; no new hard gate or score.
systemUse.System2: Candidate slow-moving industry-state vector that may condition other factors after PIT/OOS validation.
